( Disciplinary Counsel v. Frank Jacobs, 109 Ohio St.3d 252, 2006-Ohio-2292 ) John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) is the managing partner of Procopio, Cory, Hargreaves & Savitch, LLP (“Procopio”). John Alessio confirmed his legal representation of Dr. Zubie Moorjani (Medical Board #35.034433, Emeritus) on September 20, 2021. As Dr. Zubie Moorjani's attorney, John Alessio should know that Frank Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 11310) has a disciplinary history (dual representation). At inception, John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) was the sole attorney of record in San Diego Superior Court Case Number 37-2021-00033119-CU-OR-CTL. John Alessio and Sunil Moorjani are former classmates at the University of San Diego Law School (’94). As a member of the California bar, John Alessio should have recognized the conflict of interest, and he should have declined to represent the defendants. John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) made false statements to Mary Wright (California Bar No. 142886) more than four (4) months after the Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani elder abuse notification on May 20, 2021. John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) made false statements to Mary Wright (California Bar No. 142886) more than four (4) months after Dr. Zubie Moorjani's statements on May 18, 2021. Frank Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 11310) and John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) have fiduciary positions. Frank Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 11310) and John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) have undue influence. The Motion to Disqualify John Alessio  et al. provides further detail. (Note: Communications from Procopio staff are attributed to John Alessio.) Supplementary Quotes John Sheldon (Rockefeller Capital) : "Deepak Moorjani has somewhat limited patience with individuals who struggle with the complexities of  multidimensional analytical challenges ." Dr. Zubie Moorjani (Riverside Hospital) : "My dearest DEE. The last few weeks have been very stressful to you, starting from relocation, moving from New York to San Diego and now to San Francisco.  This was absolutely the wrong time to add another trauma . That's why after I realised or suspected what might be going on in Phoenix - I could not inform you right away. I wanted you to settle down a bit you - said about 10-15 days. I am sorry - you had to be told this way on phone. After my suspicions were confronted with looking at telephone statement, I had to take quick action. From my experience in the past, I felt I could not confront verbally because he might lose control or give me a silent treatment. I had planned to move to my hospital room any way before he arrived from Phoenix and wait for his response. But 8 days of turmoil took toll on my body and I got quick sick - so the doctor thought I should be admitted, rested and recuperated. Today I am being discharged. I feel great after the rest and caring nursing staff that took care of me. I have a lot of friends who care for me here. My supervisor has given me the whole week off. I don't have to go to work til Monday AM till July 6th. I have already booked my airline ticket from Aug 1st to Aug 8th to  San Diego . I got it very cheap and senior discount etc. After I talked to you Sunil called me at 12AM your time for I had left a message for him. He mentioned your e-mail. I am looking at this as a challenge and now able to deal with it as a growing experience with positive feelings . . . I am counting my blessings - my good health, physical fitness, my two great sons and a lot of friends who love me." Dr. Zubie Moorjani (Riverside Hospital): "Guloo. You need to know that I know for a fact that you have been in constant communication with your first love - Pushpa - for months. After discovering this I have gone through a number of emotions - betrayal, disgust, shock, helplessness and panic. I am devastated, feel cheated and violated. I feel like a fool. I have hardly slept since you left. As much as I find it hard to believe, you have done this. I am managing to come to grips with it. We both agree to give up our retirement home. I had so looked forward to living there even before I had seen it. When I saw the place in 1997 Feb, it was so beautiful - more than I ever imagined. It broke my heart to give it up, even more. We made a decision to build and sell only because it would have been so uncomfortable being and living so close to this woman. In spite of this, I have found now you have carried on with this relationship without due regard to my feelings - me your wife of 33 years. It's absolutely mindboggling. You have so masterfully hidden it from me. My faith in you is completely shattered. After what has happened, I will always question the TRUTH and sincerity of actions and words. I cannot bear to live with you under conditions you have created. I cannot even face you . . . I hope in future, we will be able to communicate as friends for the sake of our two wonderful children. I have no intention of telling them anything on the phone. DEE is in state of transition. I hope and pray you won't either. They need to be told about this face to face at one time." Dr. Zubie Moorjani (Riverside Hospital): "My dear sons, I don't know exactly where to begin. Initially I wanted to tell you, the news, in person when I came there in August. But I realise waiting till August will be too late. The enclosed copy of the letter, I left for Dad, will explain why I did what I did. I could not face Dad after I realised or found out the information mentioned it in, at least for a while. Finally I wanted some control and some say. I have a nice room at the hospital. I am fine. I have a lot of support emotional and spiritual from my friends. Please don't worry about me." Dr. Zubie Moorjani (Riverside Hospital): "My dearest sons, I don't know exactly where to begin. I was waiting till August to tell you in person at one time. But now I feel one month is too long. So I am writing to you, now to share with you the most difficult decision I have made in my life. I love you both so much and feel the love you have for me, as your mother. It is very important for me to know that both of you understand and support my decision and still continue embracing me as your mother and confidant . . . We have 24 hour security in hospital & I am safe." Geraldine Fabrikant (The New York Times): "Father William LeRoux, Michael Hindery and his mother, Marie, could not recall a stint by Leo Hindery Junior in the merchant marine. Confronted with these discrepancies late last week, Leo Hindery Junior said that his recollections of events that took place decades ago were less benign than those of others, and he stood by his accounts of a difficult childhood. "I never exaggerate about that," he said. And he insisted that he had spent several summers working on a ship called the U.S.S. Avila off the Northwest coast. 'The past hurts, and I don't like it,' Leo Hindery Junior said." Deepak's Note: Leo Hindery Senior served on the U.S.S. Enterprise in World War II. Leo Hindery Junior (former Global Crossing CEO) : "I know people. I know them better than anyone knows them. I don't talk about it much, but I never make mistakes . . . I started paying for everything in my life when I was 9 years old. I used to work in the fields, and I would give the money to my family, partly because that was how my family worked and partly because I was so mad at them. I had a such a crummy childhood. You just can't know how cruel my parents were. Nobody beat me, but there was just a total absence of affection. I got a Christmas gift once. It was a belt, a size 38 belt. I weighed about 125 pounds." Geraldine Fabrikant (The New York Times): " Marie Hindery  acknowledges that she has had her share of emotional problems. In telephone interviews, she said she suffered from the eating disorders of anorexia and bulimia, had low self-esteem and was estranged from all three of her children (Leo Hindery Junior, Michael Hindery, Mary Ann Seiwerath)." Leo Hindery Junior (former Global Crossing CEO): "I have done what I set out to do at Global Crossing – improve operating management and rationalize operating assets, realize the value of Global Center, and meet or exceed quarterly financial goals." Robert Pirie  (Rothschild Inc.): " Deepak Moorjani  is a very talented former colleague of mine with extensive venture capital experience." Sonia Loya (First American): "Dr. Zubie Moorjani, you can certainly quitclaim your interest to your son. I am not qualified to advise you as to what you need to do, however you are welcome to talk to one of our Title officers that can help you. Marie Castillo 619)231-4649, Korey Mulvey 619)231-4670. Have a wonderful Christmas!" Michael Spindler (Apple) : "After 30 years in corporate life, I decided to work in private equity, and I co-founded and co-managed Upstart Capital with  Deepak Moorjani  - he came highly recommended by former colleagues of mine. At Upstart Capital, I got to know Deepak quite well personally and professionally. Deepak is a great talent for the position at hand and an equally great human being - two qualities which, together, you do not find that often in an individual these days." Deepak's Note: After Apple, Michael Spindler served on the boards and advisory boards of media conglomerate Bertelsmann AG, German carmaker Daimler-Benz, and biomedical and medical device startups. He became a venture capitalist at Upstart Capital, and he served as a trustee to non-profit organizations (American Film Institute in Los Angeles and Libraries for the Future in New York). Mark Bronson (Skadden Arps) : "Deepak Moorjani has a most illustrious private equity career." Joichi Ito (Neoteny): "Deepak, I really would like you to meet one of my best friends Vibhav. He works between India and Japan and is very influential. His family has been doing some new business including deals that involve a need for someone with your sort of background. I think that maybe you would make a good fit. Vibhav is in town until the 1st or the 2nd, but maybe you two can hook up. - Joi" Karamjit Kalsi (Morgan Stanley): "Fred and Deepak, Very compelling. Let's do work on these resi JREITs and buy shares in all and then initiate dialogue." Leo Hindery Junior (former Global Crossing CEO) (cc: Mark Coleman (California Bar No. 111061)): "Dear Deepak, Ironically, I was just admitted last week, and it really is an honor, which I highly recommend to you. The Council would be lucky to have you, and vice versa, especially as your career is still at a relatively young stage. In other words, go for it. As for Morgan Stanley, make sure your orbit includes both Paul Taubman and Jeff Hogan, who are decent, bright and clear leaders of the next generation of the Firm. Always let me know if you are coming to New York. Kindest regards, Leo" David Fann (Aksia LLC): "Kunna - My friend Deepak Moorjani of Morgan Stanley thought that you would be interested in our strategy. We acquire 'small cap' U.S. based technology companies that we believe are either relevant or prospectively relevant to Asia.  Post acquisition, we move certain business operations such as manufacturing, research and development, and administration to Asia.  Longer term, we intend to create growth opportunities in Asia directly and through corporate partnerships.  As you'll see in our presentation, the team has the skills and experience to execute on this strategy. I've attached a copy of our presentation for your review. I will call you in two weeks to follow-up on your thoughts." Chief Justice Thomas Moyer (Ohio Supreme Court) : "I would suspend Frank David Jacobs for six months and stay the suspension on the condition that he commit no further misconduct during that term." ( Disciplinary Counsel v. Frank David Jacobs, 109 Ohio St.3d 252, 2006-Ohio-2292) . Deepak's Note: On August 11, 2005, relator, Disciplinary Counsel, filed an amended complaint charging respondent with professional misconduct. A panel of the Board of Commissioners on Grievances and Discipline considered the case on the parties' consent-to-discipline agreement, see Section 11 of the Rules and Regulations Governing Procedure on Complaints and Hearings Before the Board of Commissioners on Grievances and Discipline ("BCGD Proc.Reg.") and made findings of misconduct and a recommendation, which the board adopted. Jun Makihara (Neoteny Ltd.) : "My college roommate and best friend (Michael Cohrs) is head of Deutsche Bank's Investment Bank, of which you would be a part, but that gives me no insight into their strategy, etc. Lehman, I think, is a better overall firm, but joining Deutsche Bank might allow you more leeway to build a business . . ." Kenji Natsuyama (Deutsche Bank): "Thank you, Deepak, but I could not see the attachment. Would you resend?" Jennifer Compton (Sun Federal): "Deepak, Thank you for contacting me. I am excited to hear that you would like to become a member of the Credit Union. I have a website you can log onto that showcases our products and services. It is www.sunfcu.org. Also, regarding your mother's account (Dr. Moorjani) I am unable to release any information without her permission. I would need her to sign an authorization in order to give you the payoff on her mortgage. I know that you would like this to be a surprise for her; however I am unable to comply with your request without her knowing. I look forward to doing business with you. Thank you." Jennifer Compton (Sun Federal): "Good morning, Your mom called me today and gave her permission to release her mortgage payoff information: To pay her mortgage in full the amount is: $127,442.01. This payoff is good thru 12/17/06" Jennifer Compton (Sun Federal): "Deepak, I have received the wire and your mother's mortgage has been paid in full. Have a wonderful Holiday and I hope to work with you more in the future." Michael Cohrs (Deutsche Bank): "At the beginning of the meeting, Deepak was concerned why Legal, HR and Compliance have his letter to Michael Cohrs. Kimura-san explained the letter was sent to Global Head of Legal (Richard Walker) from Michael Cohrs as business is not able to make any investigation for his case, and then legal called HR for Compensation and other issue, and Compliance for FSA issue to this meeting. It is also mentioned that this case is handled as "strictly confidential" basis and no one has any knowledge about it except for Mitchell Mason (Tokyo), Henry Ritchotte (Tokyo) and relevant regional head of HR (Rachel Blanshard), Legal (Mark Grolman) and Compliance (Andrew Hume)." (Michael Cohrs, Deutsche Bank, Exhibit 14) Mark Grolman (Deutsche Bank Australia) to  Richard Walker (New York Bar No. 1377324) : "Below are draft notes of the interview I had with Frank Forelle yesterday. NEXT STEPS. I suggest for your consideration that the next steps should be: (a) we interview Sunil Madan. Tom Kimura has agreed to do that by telephone as soon as possible this week; (b) when Deepak Moorjani returns to Tokyo from the US next week, we press him again to produce all evidence he has of any alleged violations or wrongdoing. In the two weeks since he was interviewed he has not produced any evidence; (c) agree a letter to Mr Moorjani in response to his letter. I suggest that this letter be signed by David Hatt as President and CEO of DSI (the employer of Mr. Moorjani). David Hatt has been briefed on this matter. I will draft a response letter for your review. Once agreed, that letter should be delivered to Mr. Moorjani. I also propose giving the draft notes of meeting to Frank Forelle to check for accuracy." Julia Bates (Lucas County Prosecutor) : " Anthony Pizza  was a hero. He was a tremendous mentor. He was a fierce fighter of crime. He was loving to his family. I guess his legacy is incredible. His legacy will survive as one of greatness, an advocate of victims, and truly a scholar of law." Doug Solomon (IDEO): Hi D, So sorry for the big hassle and upset. I agree totally with Leo Hindery's analysis and recommend that you start looking for a new job and get out of that environment. I also don't recommend a law suit, but, of course that is up to you. There are few attorneys who will represent individuals against corporations. I know of two who are excellent. I'd recommend that you contact Eric Kastner in Palo Alto. He is good, nice to work with, tough and very experienced with many employee/employer issues in the Valley and beyond. He is a bit expensive (around $400/hr as I recall) but that is about what all good attorneys charge. His email is: eck@kastnerbanchero.com and his phone is 650 967-7854 x113. Hope this helps. Let me know how it goes. Best, d" Kenji Natsuyama (Deutsche Bank): "PLEASE CALL." Andrew Morse (The Wall Street Journal): "Hey deepak, Sorry to hear about your problems. In KL right now but let's get together when I get back. Hang in there. Andrew" Peter Coney (Herbert Smith): "Hi Peter Godwin, Please see below. I am happy to pick up on my return but is it possible for someone else to deal in my absence (assuming we want to take this on - I must say it looks like an interesting case and may be a good one to try out Nakanishi on assuming he can pay our fees)." Peter Godwin (Herbert Smith): "Hi Deepak, Peter Coney is presently away from the office (returning on Thursday) so he has asked me to respond on his behalf. I head our dispute resolution practice which includes employment issues such as that which you face. I should say that we at Herbert Smith will not be able to go on the  record as acting for you against Deutsche Bank.  Whilst we do not act for them in Japan so there is certainly no legal conflict, they are a major client of the firm in other jurisdictions.  That said, if you would still like to speak with us, I would be pleased to speak with you and understand a little more about the issues you are facing.  If you wished, we could then perhaps stand behind your Japanese counsel to stress test the advice you are receiving and assist you with strategy. If this works for you, please do call me on 03 5412 5412. I should be around today until about 3:15pm after which I will be in external meetings." John Markoff (The New York Times): "Hi Deepak, Good to hear from you. The Times New Bureau in SF is at the address below. best, John" Andrew Morse (The Wall Street Journal): "Hey deepak, Nice to run into you on the street the other day. Understand wholly your trepidation at speaking openly about things in front of someone you don't know. Listen, I checked my mail box and I can't find anything from you. It's possible it got filed into someone else's, but that's unlikely. Maybe you could resend it? Hope all's well, andrew" John Markoff (The New York Times): "Hi Deepak, Sorry for being a lousy correspondent. In looking at your documents it seems like your best bet at the Times is our Tokyo business correspondent Martin Fackler. Should I introduce you? send the documents on to him? best, John" Peter Godwin (Herbert Smith): "Dear Deepak, Thanks very much for your note. Your former employer is playing 'hard-ball' and we agree with you that at this stage it appears the only way now to get things moving toward a satisfactory resolution is to commence legal proceedings. As you know, your former employer is an existing client of Herbert Smith's offices outside Japan. Accordingly, if we are to assist you in the legal proceedings, we request that you not mention our name or involvement to your former employer. We trust that is satisfactory. Second, because this will be a Japanese proceeding Japanese counsel will need to be engaged to represent you in court (with us assisting with strategy 'behind the scenes'). We will source for you the most appropriate Japanese counsel for this case. We should add that your case has recently taken on something of a 'profile'. We have heard in the market about the union activities at the Deutsche Bank Christmas party. Assuming you are happy with the above arrangements, we are happy to assist you in preparing in conjunction with Japanese counsel a statement of claim to file against your former employer. To enable us to commence work, we would request, as we do with individual clients in court proceedings such as this, a payment in advance for our fees to our client trust account of JPY2 million. Our account details are as follows: - Account Name: Herbert Smith Gaikokuho Jimu Bengoshi Jimusho. Mizuho Bank Toranomon Branch (046). Futsu Account No. 2660480. We will then be happy to meet with you at a time of your convenience and then to obtain all necessary documents and information so that the statement of claim can be prepared and filed as soon as possible. As to your questions, there is nothing preventing you from stopping your union activities once you commence legal proceedings. Perhaps this, together with your question regarding 'outside help', is something we can discuss when we meet (and as to your second email today - yes, we are happy for the first meeting to be a general discussion of the case so you can put a 'face' to Peter Coney's name). We look forward to hearing from you. Best, Peter Godwin/Peter Coney" Richard Walker (Deutsche Bank AG) : "I have concluded that I should resign from MBIA’s Board. I do so with great regret and only after very careful consideration of the interests of both MBIA and Deutsche Bank. When I joined MBIA’s Board in 2006, existing business relationships between MBIA and Deutsche Bank provided no basis to believe that I would be unable to give both institutions my full attention and undivided loyalty. Given the events of the past week, however, I am now in a position where I can no longer be confident that continuing to act on behalf of both institutions will not lead to the possibility of an appearance that I may have reason to favor one over the other on a matter of great importance to both. In these circumstances, my ability to continue to act on behalf of either institution may be constrained. Given the importance of restoring credibility in the marketplace, I would not want my role to become a distraction to ongoing efforts to achieve this goal." Taka Hyuga (Bloomberg): "Dear Deepak-san, Hi, Deepak. Thanks for calling me the other day. I booked a table at a French place Monna Lisa at Marunouchi Building (36 floor) for noon. If you prefer Italian or Thai food, please let me know. I can easily change." Taka Hyuga (Bloomberg): "Deepak, Hi, good to see you today. Sorry I left early. I sent you the (David Hatt) story as fyi. Stay in touch. I will also send you details on the labour union I mentioned. Have a good weekend! Taka" Andrew Morse (The Wall Street Journal): "Hmm... Someone sent me a copy. I haven't read it yet, but I'll probably have a japanese colleague scan over it on monday. Good luck." Taka Hyuga (Bloomberg): "Hi, Deepak. I received the documents. I read through it, and I think you can win. Can I see your lawyer urgently? Can I contact her? Taka Hyuga" Nancy Yamaguchi (California Bar No. #213143) : "Hi (redacted) -- hope you are doing well. I've been busy going back and forth between Europe and Silicon Valley lately, and I've been spending a lot of time in London and Frankfurt. Too bad my new job does not take me to Japan. Most of the work has been in Europe. I'm enjoying the new job and feel that my decision to leave Jones Day was a good one. Recently, I was promoted to be the senior M&A lawyer for my company, and it has been great working closely with the executives as well as various outside counsel. At Jones Day, my mentors were the partners that I worked for, but at my current job, the Chief Legal Officer is an amazingly gifted lawyer and I have the chance to work with top partners at many different law firms. Are you still at Deutsche Bank? It seems like a great opportunity, and I hope that you are having fun. It's great that you are helping Deepak there. He is a successful venture capitalist in Silicon Valley and well-connected international business player. At some point, I expect that he will be back in California and restart his venture capital/private equity and M&A practice. He is a very smart guy and will be an important technology leader and dealmaker, so I'm sure he will remember your supporting him at Deutsche Bank. You should also continue building the relationship with Deepak because you may want to work with him in Silicon Valley or other international markets in the future. I would be excited to see both you and Deepak here in California. I also want to congratulate you for upholding justice and acting with utmost professional integrity. It is essential that international lawyers like you and me do the right thing. Now that I am inside a company, I am frequently preventing business people from doing what they want, but I have a professional and ethical duty to force them to take legal compliance seriously, and it can get difficult sometimes. I believe that in the end, justice will always prevail and wrongdoers eventually fall -- a good example is Enron and all of the executives and investment bankers who are now going to jail and whose careers are ruined for life. I personally saw a lot of this happening when I worked on a SEC investigation of certain accounting practices at telecommunication/Internet companies. It was alarming to see many lawyers and accountants lose their jobs and careers, but also the civil and criminal penalties were severe. As lawyers, our first and foremost professional obligation is to advise business people to follow the law and to act in a fair and just manner. Legal compliance is not always easy, but that is our job and we chose to become lawyers. If we take the easy road and simply follow the business people's desires, we would fail as lawyers and have no choice but to resign. Such professional failure would also result in losing the license to practice law or disbarment, and definitely a loss of professional credibility and careers. In any case, I'm glad to see that you are doing the right thing by helping Deepak and please continue to help him -- of course, it is your professional duty as a lawyer, but I also want you to know that I appreciate and respect you for it." John Markoff (The New York Times): "Hi Deepak, I will forward this to Martin Fackler. best, John" Paul Barrett (BusinessWeek): "Deepak: Thanks for your email. With your permission, I'll pass it along to a colleague more expert than I in finance to get his opinion. As I mentioned, I've moved (back) to BusinessWeek magazine as assistant managing editor for investigative projects, so that's where I'd explore potential coverage. I'm not really in the business of offering advice on media strategies, generally. But if you offer your story exclusively to BusinessWeek, we would certainly entertain seriously the idea of writing about your experiences. My guess is that we'd be interested in an "inside story" of life within a major investment bank in a time of crisis. It goes without saying that by telling us this story candidly, you would in all likelihood be burning bridges at DB and possibly in the industry generally. I wouldn't always necessarily offer that reminder, but since you approach me as a friend of Omid Safi (FOM?), and I owe him a debt of gratitude for helping me with past work on unrelated matters, I want to make sure you've thought this through. Let me know whether I can share your letter. Also, have you formally filed suit? If so, we'd want to see your legal papers. Best wishes (and sorry about the unhappiness that leads to your contacting me), Paul" Leo Hindery Junior (former Global Crossing CEO): "I would love to see you, Deepak, but I will be in Korea with our Defense and State Departments on behalf of Obama.  I will miss seeing you. Leo" Chris Hughes (The Financial Times): "Dear Mr Moorjani, Thank you for your email. Please could you contact me at your earliest convenience on +44 20 7873 4318. Regards, Chris Hughes" Matthew Goldstein (BusinessWeek): "Deepak, Hi. I think for now, it doesn't make sense to do a story for BusinessWeek. I'm not passing judgment on the merits of your case; it's just I don't see a bigger picture here for our readers. To do a story, I'd like to see alleged violations that paint a real systemic problem at Deutsche Bank. If your allegations are true, I see some problems with the Asian operation, but not on a large enough scale. By all means, let me know how your case turns out. Best, Doug Solomon" Deepak Moorjani (to  Brigid Heid, Ohio Bar No. 47142 ): "Eastman & Smith have obtained and have used our personal data without our knowledge and without our consent. Eastman & Smith’s previous uses of our personal data constitute willful violations, and Eastman & Smith’s retention of our personal data is expressly prohibited. Brigid Heid of Eastman & Smith shall promptly deliver a notarized affidavit certifying the deletion of our personal data by all members of Eastman & Smith. Further, Brigid Heid of Eastman & Smith shall disclose the identities of any persons to whom our personal data was disclosed. This notarized affidavit shall be delivered to Zubie Moorjani, M.D. in Sylvania, Ohio. This notarized affidavit shall also include: i) the specifics of Frank Jacobs' restraining order, and ii) the precautionary measures taken by any member(s) of Eastman & Smith subsequent to the January 08, 2019 suicide red flag raised by Jennifer Compton of Sun Federal Credit Union. Eastman & Smith were notified of this suicide red flag in a January 10, 2019 letter delivered to Louise Jackson of Eastman & Smith . . . Based on the facts and circumstances, the primary issue seems to be Frank Jacobs' competence."  Deepak Moorjani: "Hi Mom, I forgive you for your poor behavior, and I love you unconditionally. I would like you to participate in your own rescue." Deepak Moorjani : "This memorandum is an official notification of Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani’s  elder abuse ." Deepak Moorjani : "Hi Seema, The attached recordings demonstrate your mother-in-law's state of mind and her state of health. One was taken at 3:57pm PST, and the other was taken at 4:12pm PST. Note: The recordings were made on May 18, 2021." Deepak Moorjani: "Hi Jennifer, I spoke with Adult Protection Services in Lucas County, and I gave your name as one of the references. Here are the issues that they might consider: (i) an inability to handle personal finances, (ii) exploitation: my mom's inability to live in her house in San Diego, because Sunil and his wife (Seema) will not allow her, (iii) recent hospitalization: last month's broken pelvis, and (iv) previous interventions: the Jan 08, 2019 suicide red flag that you correctly raised (but was ignored by most). Have a great weekend. Deepak" Deepak Moorjani : "Hi Seema, On May 22, 2021, I emailed two audio recordings to Seema Moorjani which demonstrate my mom's lack of competence. Subsequently, Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani changed my mom's phone number in order to isolate my mom further. Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani are actively seeking to exploit my mom's lack of competence. Until May 22, 2021, my mom's cellphone number was 858.226.6036. The attached May 24, 2021 audio recording demonstrates that my mom's phone number has been changed. My mom does not have the ability to change her number: my mom's cellphone service is controlled by Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani. This is not a one-time event, but this demonstrates a pattern of  elder abuse . Previously, my mom's cellphone was 858.353.6731. Subsequent to Jennifer Compton's suicide red flag on January 08, 2019, Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani changed my mom's cellphone number from 858.353.6731 to 858.226.6036 without notification." Sunita Karnani (Sylvania, Ohio) : "I am not in touch with your mother anymore. She moved to California." Deepak Moorjani: "On August 25, 2021 at 1:02pm, the Lucas County Sheriff served Zubeida Moorjani at 6036 Quarrys Edge Lane, Sylvania, Ohio 43560-9877. On September 12, 2021, Sunita Karnani informed me that 'she moved to California.' While I consider this move to be an admission of liability, I deliver this Offer to Mediate." John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900): "Hi Oriet Cohen-Supple – Nice to meet you via e-mail. I wanted to reach out and introduce myself, as well as confirm that you are representing Deepak Moorjani. I am attaching our meet and confer letter regarding our clients’ intended demurrer. Are you able to let me know by Friday whether your client intends to dismiss? Thank you." (to Mary Wright (Bar No. 142886) and Oriet Cohen-Supple (Bar No. 206781)) Deepak Moorjani (to  Brigid Heid, Ohio Bar No. 47142 ): "Do you agree that Frank Jacobs’ conduct demonstrates his elder abuse of Zubeida Moorjani? At the time of his request, did Frank Jacobs have a preexisting professional relationship with Jennifer Compton? Did Eastman & Smith have a preexisting professional relationship with Sun Federal Credit Union? Do you agree that Frank Jacobs’ request to Jennifer Compton demonstrates his willful misconduct? In  Disciplinary Counsel v. Frank Jacobs , the nominal decision was 4-3, but the effective decision was 7-0. Three judges dissented, because they believed that Frank Jacobs of Eastman & Smith should have received a harsher penalty." Michael Charles Ferguson (California Bar No. 42797): "Hi James. It's great to hear from you, as always. It would be great to see you again. We're leaving 10/20 for 3 weeks in Italy, but will be back 11/12-so anytime after that. Re: your friends: the first thing to do is to report the situation to Adult Protective Services in the County in which the parents live. Here are the links for Alameda and Contra Costa Counties, respectively: https://www.alamedacountysocialservices.org/our-services/Abuse-and-Protection/adult-and-senior-abuse/index https://www.contracosta.ca.gov/914/Adult-Protective-Services Re an attorney to help: I'd suggest you contact Kathryn Korn in Orinda. Here's the link to her website: https://www.kornlawgroup.com/ I hope this helps. Let me know if you have other questions. Warmest regards, Mike" John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) : "Hi Oriet Cohen-Supple – The reason why you received the response you did is a product of Deepak’s own doing. His  consistent harassment of Zubie, family, and friends  over the last decade has left everyone feeling deeply concerned and emotionally distressed about what he might do next. Our clients will not sit back and continue to suffer any longer. For example, in 2014, Deepak sent a package to his mother demanding she sign a power of attorney in his favor, and threatened to file a court action alleging her incompetence with a goal of appointing him as her legal guardian. Zubie’s attorney in Ohio (Frank Jacobs) sent him an e-mail stating Zubie told him Deepak had been very aggressive towards her to the point of being not only insulting, but abusive and overbearing.  Frank Jacobs (Eastman & Smith)  relayed Zubie’s wish that Deepak was not welcome at her home, the locks were changed, and should he attempt to enter the premises the police would be called. That directive remains, and should Deepak (directly or indirectly) attempt to visit our clients for any reason, we will seek a civil harassment restraining order against him immediately due to his continued course of conduct to harass our clients. No undue influence is being exerted over Zubie, and her physician has once again recently certified that she is competent to handle her affairs. The bottom line is Deepak must stay away. If he insists on proceeding with his meritless lawsuit and/or threatened  elder abuse claims , which is based on nothing more than rank conjecture, our clients will vigorously defend them and use any and all means available to seek recourse from the Court. I would encourage you to fully vet claims he may wish to file before actually doing so. Notwithstanding the above, and if your client agrees to drop his claims, our clients are willing to provide the physician’s finding of competence and a notarized statement from Zubie declaring her wish that she does not want Deepak to be a part of her life, and that he should cease attempting to contact her." (to Mary Wright (Bar No. 142886) and Oriet Cohen-Supple (Bar No. 206781)) Deepak's Note to (i) The Office of Disciplinary Counsel (The Supreme Court of Ohio) and (ii) The Office of Chief Trial Counsel (The State Bar of California): On September 20, 2021, John Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) confirmed his legal representation of Dr. Zubie Moorjani (Medical Board #35.034433, Emeritus). On May 25, 2021, I filed a report in Lucas County, Ohio for (i) neglect and abandonment and (ii) financial abuse . . . These issues are described in the attached First Amended Complaint; this has been filed as a part of San Diego Superior Court Case No. 37-2021-00033119-CU-OR-CTL." Deepak Moorjani: "On November 19, 2021, I called Adult Protective Services (“APS”) in San Diego to request an investigation on the elder abuse of Zubeida Moorjani. My mother is an elder person who is a retired medical doctor. On November 19, 2021, I spoke with Pam (intake) at 800.399.2021. Based on our conversation, Pam believed that an investigation would commence based on (i) emotional abuse and (ii) financial abuse. On November 19, 2021, I mailed written information to APS in San Diego, and this letter provides additional information . . . Additionally, I would like APS of San Diego to investigate John Alessio (Bar No. 174900) for elder abuse. The attached Notification: Suicide Risk is dated January 10, 2019, and this letter was sent via certified mail to Rosemarie Osowik, MD with a cc: to Jennifer Compton of Sun Federal, Louise Jackson of Eastman & Smith, and Sunil Moorjani. Additional, this letter was sent via certified mail to Thomas Osowik, a judge in the Ohio Sixth District Court of Appeals. Despite the filing of the First Amended Compliant (Elder Abuse Petition), John Alessio and Procopio have still failed to recuse themselves; consequently, I filed a Notice of Motion and Motion to Disqualify, a Memorandum of Points and Authority, and a Declaration of Plaintiff. The San Diego Superior Court Case No. 37-2021-00033119-CU-OR- CTL is being heard in C-65 by Honorable Ronald F. Frazier. In the Motion to Disqualify, John Alessio and Procopio’s emails have been produced, and John Alessio and Procopio’s emails show that they have consistently sought to force a dismissal with prejudice. However, John Alessio has client relationships with Gulab Moorjani, Seema Moorjani, Sunil Moorjani and Zubeida Moorjani. In his November 30, 2021 email (attached), one of John Alessio’s junior associates admits that the First Amended Complaint has been filed; however, the junior associate (Zagros Bassirian, Bar No. 299581) is actively soliciting a settlement proposal." Currently, John Alessio is serving his second three-year term as the managing partner of Procopio, an AmLaw 200 firm with 180+ lawyers in Del Mar Heights, Las Vegas, Orange County, Palo Alto, San Diego and Scottsdale. My client takes this step in good faith and hopes that it will lead to a cooperative and constructive dialogue with your clients regarding the future care of  Zubeida Moorjani ." Officer Travis Whitmore (Rossford Police Department) : "Caller advised he is currently trying to report elder abuse for his mother, since his brother won't let her live in her house in California. Called stated he wanted a report to show a pattern of abuse. Caller lives in California, Mother lives in California, and Father lives in Florida. I attempted to call the Mother and did not get an answer. I then spoke with Father, and he denied all allegations."

description: Center for Research and Security Studies Transcription Series: Sabawoon Program: Jarga Maraka Topic: Children Enrolment Campaign by Provincial Government Date: 13-04-2015 Guest#1: Jamaluddin (Focal Person Enrolment Campaign) Guest#2: Umar Orakzai (Provincial Coordinator Alif Ailan Organization working for improvement in Education sector) Field Story 1: Launching Ceremony of âGhar Aya Ustadâ (Teacher comes home) campaign in Peshawar (Reporter Inamullah) Field Story 2: The state of schools in Swat district (Reporter Anwar Anjum) Anchor Person: Shahabuddin Co-Anchor Person: Additional Info: Summary: The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government has launched enrolment campaign âGhar aya Ustadâ (Teacher comes home) under the auspices of Alif Ailan Organization. The campaign will be run in all parts of the province especially in rural areas. According to unofficial reports, almost 2.5 million children are out of school in the province. Approximately 70% students are studying at government schools while 30% are enrolled in private schools and Madrassas (seminaries). The campaign aims to bring students back to schools, who dropped out due to various reasons and the governmentâs target is to enroll 0.8 million children by the end of this year. For the first time, teachers and Jirga members are involved in the process, who will convince parents and guardians to send their children for schooling. In analystâs opinion parents, teachers, ruling and political elite should own this responsibility to educate each and every child of the country. They stressed upon the educated people to come forward and make this campaign a success, since illiteracy and ignorance is basic reason behind many social ills. Educating the future builders is a prerequisite for building a healthy and progressive society. Shahab: Mr. Umar Orakzai, what are the aims and objectives of Alif Ailan Organization? What kind of support it is providing to the government? Umar Orakzai: Government started children enrolment campaign recently as well as to ensure teacherâs presence in all government schools of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. As far as our organizationâs objectives is concerned, it is operational for creating awareness among the people by having sessions with them to convince them for sending children to schools. Almost 2.5 million children are out of school in the province. The organization is supporting government in cope with missing facilities in schools. Most of the parents of out of school children have the confession that due to poverty they cannot bear education expenses of their children. We aware them that government provides free education and books to their children in all public schools. Shahab: Mr. Jamaluddin, would you like to inform our listeners about âGhar Aye Ustadâ (Teacher comes home) campaign? Jamaluddin: A campaign cannot become successful, unless all relevant stakeholders i.e. teacher, parent and student, are taken on board. Without involving teachers in children enrolment campaign, the desire goals cannot be achieved. Teachers visit door-to-door to convince the parents for sending their children to schools. We have set a target of enrolling 7, 90000 children by current year. Shahab: How many children are out of school in the province? What do you mean by 7, 90000 children? Jamaluddin: Actually since 1998 no national census has been conducted, thus there is no data about actual population of the country. We are not in a position to say that a specific number of kids are out of schools in the province. According to a survey of Bureau Statistic organization, around 1.1 million children are below five years in the province. Similarly data provided by IMU and EMIS, says that around 1.1 million children will be studying at public and private schools and Madrassas. About 25 to 30% kids go to private schools and Madrassa and rest of the students are enrolled in public sector schools. Annual growth rate of the population continues at 2.81 in the province and the growth rate is varied district wise. Keeping in view that growth rate, we have identified the out of school children in each district. During the campaign, special focus is being given to rural areas as compare to cities and the number of students would be increased in underutilized schools. For the first time school head masters and district education officers are involved in the drive as the target cannot be achieved without their support. Each school administration is given a target of enrolling specific number of students as well as to control drop out ratio. Teachers will be rewarded on achieving the target. Umar Orakzai: Our organization (Alif Ailan) receive data from different sources like NIMS (National Information Management System) and Pakistan Bureau of Statistics and according to these institutions, around 2.5 million children aged 5 to 16 years are out of schools at present in the province. The number of children aged 5 to 15 is 7.1 million. Out of this over 4.6 million kids are enrolled in schools. As compare to other provinces, the ratio of out of school children is low in the province and it is 34%. Similarly 75% children never attended school and 25% dropped out at some stage. 29% female children were not allowed by their parents for schooling, 28% girls denied continuing their education after primary education and 13% do not go to school due to poverty. Absentee of teachers and missing facilities are also other causes of studentâs disinterest in education. If government wants to bring all out of school children back to schools, then article 25-A has to be implemented to make education free and compulsory. Report: Every government introduces new policies for promotion of education. In order to raise literacy rate, the PTI led coalition government launched children enrolment drive in the province. In this regard a colorful ceremony was held at Government Higher Secondary School No-1 City. Talking to CRSS, provincial education minister, Mr. Atif Khan said government has chalked out a comprehensive plan for bringing out-of school children back to schools. Respondent: âWe are giving special focus on enrolment drive, which is titled âGhar Aya Ustadâ (Teacher comes home). In our society teacher and Jirga members are given respect and their decision is normally not rejected. They are involved in the campaign to meet the community members and convince them for enrolling their children in schools. There are varied reports about number of out of school children in the province, but our target is to enroll 0.8 million out of school children in schools. I think without raising literacy rate, we cannot make sustainable developmentâ. Reporter: Chief Minister Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pervez Khattak graced the occasion as chief guest. He said government will make its promises true with the people. Respondent: âThrough an effective monitoring system, we came to know about devoid of basic facilities in all institutions of the province. We knew about the number of teachers and students in every institution of the province. Two days back, I chaired a meeting. I was informed that 95% teachers and students present in schools. Introducing reward and punishment system in education sector is a big change. The government has taken action against 4300 teachers for neglecting their duties whereas over 700 have been terminated. We have launched departmental inquiry against them. The government is allocating huge budget for ensuring all basic facilities to schools and in this regard 5000 bathrooms will also be built in institutions by next fiscal year. In next two or three years, people will feel a big change in the provinceâ. Reporter: A head of non-governmental organization, Ms. Fozia told about their project as under: Respondent: âAwareness rising among the parents and general community is the main purpose of our project. Besides providing a learning environment, school age going children should have to be enrolled to secure their future. Parents should take interest in solving education problems of their kids and in this regard Parents Teachers Council has to be made functionalâ. Shahab: Mr. Jamal, what target set by the government last year regarding enrolment of children? Jamaluddin: Last year the government announced to enroll 0.7 million kids and it achieved this target as per IMU report. I think census needs to be conducted, which would help us achieve our targets. Unavailability of accurate population data has created many problems for the country. It is surprising to listen that Pakistan is at No-2 in terms of out of school children in the world. However as compare to past, situation is now different and literacy rate is increasing rapidly. Shahab: Whether these 0.7 million students are still studying at schools or any drop out is reported? Jamaluddin: No drop out is reported since November 2014. Poverty is said to be biggest obstacle in achieving 100% literacy rate, but Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh like countries are also facing poverty, yet literacy rate is far better in these countries than Pakistan. In order to improve education sector in the province, teachers are being appointed on merit and school based policy. They are appointed through NTS (National Testing Service) as well as there is no transfer and posting on political basis. Resultantly 95% teachers, who were selected recently, are master degree holder. Now no secretary or officer can appoint his/her child as teacher. Umar Orakzai: No doubt maximum numbers of children are enrolled in last two years, but along with this dropout rate has also picked immensely. The reason for that is lack of space in already overburdened schools as well as the quality of education is also being declined. Still many schools in Charsadda, Nowshera and other adjacent districts, are in pathetic condition. IMU report suggests that in remote sites, female teachers do not come to schools regularly. Jamaluddin: the apathy that every new government claims that education is its first, second and third priority, but it may not be the reality. After independence, primary schools consisting of two teachers and two rooms were built. Whether successor governments didnât think about it that there would be need of atleast six rooms and six teachers in every primary school. Presently 40000 additional rooms need to be built in primary schools. Secondly there are some constituencies in the province, where still high schools for girls are not available while in some areas lack of high and primacy schools is a matter of concern. Shahab: Then why enrolment is so important, if schools and facilities in them are not available in appropriate manner? Is the object of the government just to show the world that we have no drop-out children? Jamaluddin: Missing facilities like boundary wall, electricity, safe drinking water and bathroom is the major problem and to address the issue, Rs.6 billion were allocated by the government. In case government diverts the whole budget of the province towards education sector, yet required number of schools and facilities cannot be completed. This is a gradual process and will take time. Shahab: Mr. Umar, many NGOs are restricted to paper work and holding seminars and nothing else. Practically they donât play any role for betterment of the society. Whether your organization highlights the problems before the government? Umar Orakzai: Our organization prepares distinct ranking report every year, which is aimed to show top districts of the country, in terms of educational facilities and teachers availability. The report also highlights those districts, where facilities are missing in schools. The report is then shared with ministers and concerned district officials and highlighted on media as well. Our organization is playing the role of a pressure group to pressurize government for improving education system in the country. Jamaluddin: We have developed a website that updates information about every school of the province like how many teachers a school has or what is the state of facilities in an institution. Report: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government announced new security plan for educational institutions of the province in aftermath of Peshawar School Carnage. Under this plan, schoolâs administration would provide protection to children by taking security measures in concerned schools and those schools would remain closed where security measures are not taken. In this regard police registered FIR against 47 teachers of various schools for not making security arrangements. The headmaster of Government High School Haji Baba, Mingora shared his views about this as under: Reporter: âMy name is Israruddin, we tried our level best to make security measures for the school, but unfortunately there is no coordination between the state departments. District Police Officer (DPO) gave us a deadline for arranging security in the school and five days were left in the deadline, but yet police lodged FIR against us. Police visited the school, when it was closedâ. Reporter: A head of private school, Noor Nawaz condemned action against teachers and said pressurizing teachers would have negative impacts on education of children. Respondent: âSome policies may look right to government, but it may have drawbacks as well that can affect the educational environment. Private school can install CCTV camera and barbwire schoolâs boundary walls by increasing the fee of the students, but what about public schools! They donât have any funds for raising boundary walls and providing security to schoolsâ. Reporter: President PSMA (association of private schools), Mr. Ahmad Siyal said despite making security arrangement, police tease them that would affect education activities in the region. Respondent: âSchoolâs heads and principles cooperate with the government, but Swat administration and police donât cooperate with us. Schools are being raided and teachers are mistreated, which is not acceptable to us. Police is supposed to help out us in providing protection to students, but their behavior is intolerable. It is the responsibility of the government, law enforcement agencies and police to provide protection to every citizen of the country. Governmentâs decision to equip teachers with pistols is also a wrong decision and it will convey a wrong message to childrenâ. Reporter: In this regard, district police officer Salim Marwat said as under: Respondent: âAccording to governmentâs new policy, government, police and school management would collectively make better the security of schools. Police is authorized to visit a school and see that security measures are taken or not. In case appropriate security arrangements are not made then police has right to take action against itâ. Endsâ¦ Shahab: Mr. Jamaluddin, teacherâs confession that state is responsible to provide security to students rather schoolâs management. They cannot do to raise school boundary walls, barb them wire and install CCTV cameras within limited resources. Teachers are also asked to have weapons with themselves during duty hours to fight against terrorists, in case they attack a school. In Hangu, Swabi and Kohat, some female teachers have refused to vaccinate children due to security reasons. Government not only stopped their salaries but suspended them. What is your view about these problems? Jamaluddin: Education minister of KP, Mr. Atif Khan has said so many times that teacherâs responsibility is to teach rather to provide protection to students. In majority of the schools, security measures have been taken. Government also issued Rs.2 billion for raising boundary walls of public schools to secure them. Some schools donât have funds for these arrangements, for example primary school cannot afford security guard and to raise boundary wall. But government is committed to solve these issues and ensure that all schools are made secure.

Without involving teachers in children enrolment campaign, the desire goals cannot be achieved. Teachers visit door-to-door to convince the parents for sending their children to schools. We have set a target of enrolling 7, 90000 children by current year. Shahab: How many children are out of school in the province? What do you mean by 7, 90000 children? Jamaluddin: Actually since 1998 no national census has been conducted, thus there is no data about actual population of the country. We are not in a position to say that a specific number of kids are out of schools in the province. According to a survey of Bureau Statistic organization, around 1.1 million children are below five years in the province. Similarly data provided by IMU and EMIS, says that around 1.1 million children will be studying at public and private schools and Madrassas. About 25 to 30% kids go to private schools and Madrassa and rest of the students are enrolled in public sector schools. Annual growth rate of the population continues at 2.81 in the province and the growth rate is varied district wise. Keeping in view that growth rate, we have identified the out of school children in each district. During the campaign, special focus is being given to rural areas as compare to cities and the number of students would be increased in underutilized schools. For the first time school head masters and district education officers are involved in the drive as the target cannot be achieved without their support. Each school administration is given a target of enrolling specific number of students as well as to control drop out ratio. Teachers will be rewarded on achieving the target. Umar Orakzai: Our organization (Alif Ailan) receive data from different sources like NIMS (National Information Management System) and Pakistan Bureau of Statistics and according to these institutions, around 2.5 million children aged 5 to 16 years are out of schools at present in the province. The number of children aged 5 to 15 is 7.1 million. Out of this over 4.6 million kids are enrolled in schools. As compare to other provinces, the ratio of out of school children is low in the province and it is 34%. Similarly 75% children never attended school and 25% dropped out at some stage. 29% female children were not allowed by their parents for schooling, 28% girls denied continuing their education after primary education and 13% do not go to school due to poverty. Absentee of teachers and missing facilities are also other causes of studentâs disinterest in education. If government wants to bring all out of school children back to schools, then article 25-A has to be implemented to make education free and compulsory. Report: Every government introduces new policies for promotion of education. In order to raise literacy rate, the PTI led coalition government launched children enrolment drive in the province. In this regard a colorful ceremony was held at Government Higher Secondary School No-1 City. Talking to CRSS, provincial education minister, Mr. Atif Khan said government has chalked out a comprehensive plan for bringing out-of school children back to schools. Respondent: âWe are giving special focus on enrolment drive, which is titled âGhar Aya Ustadâ (Teacher comes home). In our society teacher and Jirga members are given respect and their decision is normally not rejected. They are involved in the campaign to meet the community members and convince them for enrolling their children in schools. There are varied reports about number of out of school children in the province, but our target is to enroll 0.8 million out of school children in schools. I think without raising literacy rate, we cannot make sustainable developmentâ. Reporter: Chief Minister Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pervez Khattak graced the occasion as chief guest. He said government will make its promises true with the people. Respondent: âThrough an effective monitoring system, we came to know about devoid of basic facilities in all institutions of the province. We knew about the number of teachers and students in every institution of the province. Two days back, I chaired a meeting. I was informed that 95% teachers and students present in schools. Introducing reward and punishment system in education sector is a big change. The government has taken action against 4300 teachers for neglecting their duties whereas over 700 have been terminated. We have launched departmental inquiry against them. The government is allocating huge budget for ensuring all basic facilities to schools and in this regard 5000 bathrooms will also be built in institutions by next fiscal year. In next two or three years, people will feel a big change in the provinceâ. Reporter: A head of non-governmental organization, Ms. Fozia told about their project as under: Respondent: âAwareness rising among the parents and general community is the main purpose of our project. Besides providing a learning environment, school age going children should have to be enrolled to secure their future. Parents should take interest in solving education problems of their kids and in this regard Parents Teachers Council has to be made functionalâ. Shahab: Mr. Jamal, what target set by the government last year regarding enrolment of children? Jamaluddin: Last year the government announced to enroll 0.7 million kids and it achieved this target as per IMU report. I think census needs to be conducted, which would help us achieve our targets. Unavailability of accurate population data has created many problems for the country. It is surprising to listen that Pakistan is at No-2 in terms of out of school children in the world. However as compare to past, situation is now different and literacy rate is increasing rapidly. Shahab: Whether these 0.7 million students are still studying at schools or any drop out is reported? Jamaluddin: No drop out is reported since November 2014. Poverty is said to be biggest obstacle in achieving 100% literacy rate, but Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh like countries are also facing poverty, yet literacy rate is far better in these countries than Pakistan. In order to improve education sector in the province, teachers are being appointed on merit and school based policy. They are appointed through NTS (National Testing Service) as well as there is no transfer and posting on political basis. Resultantly 95% teachers, who were selected recently, are master degree holder. Now no secretary or officer can appoint his/her child as teacher. Umar Orakzai: No doubt maximum numbers of children are enrolled in last two years, but along with this dropout rate has also picked immensely. The reason for that is lack of space in already overburdened schools as well as the quality of education is also being declined. Still many schools in Charsadda, Nowshera and other adjacent districts, are in pathetic condition. IMU report suggests that in remote sites, female teachers do not come to schools regularly. Jamaluddin: the apathy that every new government claims that education is its first, second and third priority, but it may not be the reality. After independence, primary schools consisting of two teachers and two rooms were built. Whether successor governments didnât think about it that there would be need of atleast six rooms and six teachers in every primary school. Presently 40000 additional rooms need to be built in primary schools. Secondly there are some constituencies in the province, where still high schools for girls are not available while in some areas lack of high and primacy schools is a matter of concern. Shahab: Then why enrolment is so important, if schools and facilities in them are not available in appropriate manner? Is the object of the government just to show the world that we have no drop-out children? Jamaluddin: Missing facilities like boundary wall, electricity, safe drinking water and bathroom is the major problem and to address the issue, Rs.6 billion were allocated by the government. In case government diverts the whole budget of the province towards education sector, yet required number of schools and facilities cannot be completed. This is a gradual process and will take time. Shahab: Mr. Umar, many NGOs are restricted to paper work and holding seminars and nothing else. Practically they donât play any role for betterment of the society. Whether your organization highlights the problems before the government? Umar Orakzai: Our organization prepares distinct ranking report every year, which is aimed to show top districts of the country, in terms of educational facilities and teachers availability. The report also highlights those districts, where facilities are missing in schools. The report is then shared with ministers and concerned district officials and highlighted on media as well. Our organization is playing the role of a pressure group to pressurize government for improving education system in the country. Jamaluddin: We have developed a website that updates information about every school of the province like how many teachers a school has or what is the state of facilities in an institution. Report: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government announced new security plan for educational institutions of the province in aftermath of Peshawar School Carnage. Under this plan, schoolâs administration would provide protection to children by taking security measures in concerned schools and those schools would remain closed where security measures are not taken. In this regard police registered FIR against 47 teachers of various schools for not making security arrangements. The headmaster of Government High School Haji Baba, Mingora shared his views about this as under: Reporter: âMy name is Israruddin, we tried our level best to make security measures for the school, but unfortunately there is no coordination between the state departments. District Police Officer (DPO) gave us a deadline for arranging security in the school and five days were left in the deadline, but yet police lodged FIR against us. Police visited the school, when it was closedâ. Reporter: A head of private school, Noor Nawaz condemned action against teachers and said pressurizing teachers would have negative impacts on education of children. Respondent: âSome policies may look right to government, but it may have drawbacks as well that can affect the educational environment. Private school can install CCTV camera and barbwire schoolâs boundary walls by increasing the fee of the students, but what about public schools! They donât have any funds for raising boundary walls and providing security to schoolsâ. Reporter: President PSMA (association of private schools), Mr. Ahmad Siyal said despite making security arrangement, police tease them that would affect education activities in the region. Respondent: âSchoolâs heads and principles cooperate with the government, but Swat administration and police donât cooperate with us. Schools are being raided and teachers are mistreated, which is not acceptable to us. Police is supposed to help out us in providing protection to students, but their behavior is intolerable. It is the responsibility of the government, law enforcement agencies and police to provide protection to every citizen of the country. Governmentâs decision to equip teachers with pistols is also a wrong decision and it will convey a wrong message to childrenâ. Reporter: In this regard, district police officer Salim Marwat said as under: Respondent: âAccording to governmentâs new policy, government, police and school management would collectively make better the security of schools. Police is authorized to visit a school and see that security measures are taken or not. In case appropriate security arrangements are not made then police has right to take action against itâ. Endsâ¦ Shahab: Mr. Jamaluddin, teacherâs confession that state is responsible to provide security to students rather schoolâs management. They cannot do to raise school boundary walls, barb them wire and install CCTV cameras within limited resources. Teachers are also asked to have weapons with themselves during duty hours to fight against terrorists, in case they attack a school. In Hangu, Swabi and Kohat, some female teachers have refused to vaccinate children due to security reasons. Government not only stopped their salaries but suspended them. What is your view about these problems? Jamaluddin: Education minister of KP, Mr. Atif Khan has said so many times that teacherâs responsibility is to teach rather to provide protection to students. In majority of the schools, security measures have been taken. Government also issued Rs.2 billion for raising boundary walls of public schools to secure them. Some schools donât have funds for these arrangements, for example primary school cannot afford security guard and to raise boundary wall. But government is committed to solve these issues and ensure that all schools are made secure.

title: CIA Reading Room cia-rdp86t01017r000807950001-1: HIZBALLAH'S RISE: THE US STAKE
description: 25X1 Declassified in Part - Sanitized Copy Approved for Release 2012/05/16: CIA-RDP86T01017R000807950001-1 Central Intelligence Agency DIRECTORATE OF INTELLIGENCE 21 October 1986 Hizballah's Rise: The US Stake Summary Hizballah--a pro-Iranian Shia fundamentalist movement--has become Lebanon's most dynamic political faction. From a throng of activist groups it has become a cohesive organization able to play a major--albeit negative--role in national politics. It has the capacity to negate any reconciliation of Lebanon's warring factions. During the next few years, Israeli, Syrian, and other domestic opposition probably will prevent Hizballah from creating an Islamic Reoublic in Lebanon, but the radical group probably will wrest control of sizable parts of South Lebanon from its moderate Shia rival, Amal. The fundamentalist group already controls Ba'labakk and part of the northern 3ekaa valley with Syrian acquiescence. Hizballah's rise threatens to undermine US interests by: --promoting terrorism, particularly against American targets in the Middle East, --offering Iran a major foreign police success--the first radical Shia victory in an Arab country, This memorandum was prepared by the Levant 25X1 3ranch, Arab-Israeli Divisio Asian Analysis. Information its preparation. Questions n, Office o as of 21 O and comments r Near Eastern and South ctober 1986 was used in should be addressed to Chief, Arab-Israeli Division 25X1 25X1 Declassified in Part - Sanitized Copy Approved for Release 2012/05/16: CIA-RDP86T01017R000807950001-1 Declassified in Part - Sanitized Copy Approved for Release 2012/05/16: CIA-RDP86T01017R000807950001-1 25X1 --strengthening Shia fundamentalism throughout the region, --facilitating military and terrorist operations against Israel, --provoking Israeli-Syrian clashes, --wrecking the prospects that an independent Lebanon can emerge from the country's civil war. Hizballah's Rise Hizballah has. come of age as a political organization, relentlessly building its militia, seizing control of important territory, and expanding its political role and contacts. Before 1982, Hizballah's political presence was generally limited to vocal but nonviolent demonstrations. The Israeli invasion galvanized Lebanon's Shias, and motivated otherwise fractious 25X1 Shia groups to cooperate. Guidance and support from Tehran accelerated Hizballah's development, as did. the lack of any authoritative or respected Lebanese voice to stop them. In late 1982, Hizballah seized the Shaykh Abdallah Barracks in Ba'labakk from the Lebanese Army beginning the radical-Shia control of Lebanese territory. 25X1 Hizballah military strength puts it on a par with Lebanon's other major militias.
